name: # The rows that pin repaired divergences, and the controls and
# neighbours measured with them: each case with the one answer every
# runtime gives since the repair. The register proves a split is live.
# This file proves it stays closed, through the same probes and the same
# runners, ts/test/divergent.test.js, go/divergent_test.go and
# rs/tests/divergent_spec_test.rs. A register row comes here by dropping
# two of its three runtime columns and its justification; a control or a
# neighbour that was measured with a repair and never registered, because
# the runtimes already agreed on it or because the repair landed with the
# measurement, is written here directly. FIVE tab-separated columns:
#   name      unique, kebab-case; a row that was in the register keeps its
#             name, so the DIVERGENCE.md entry under "Repaired, and what
#             replaced them" can still cite it
#   probe     `lex` or `spec`, as divergent.tsv defines them
#   arg       the probe's arguments, as divergent.tsv spells them
#   input     the source text
#   expected  what EVERY runtime produces since the repair
# A `# @repaired:` line names the DIVERGENCE.md entry its rows pin: the
# entry a register group left, or a repair recorded only under
# "Repaired". That entry must not be a `### ` heading there and must be
# mentioned under "Repaired": go/divergent_test.go checks both, and that
# no name here is also a row name in divergent.tsv. A row that fails here
# is a repaired divergence coming back. It belongs in divergent.tsv again,
# with its entry, not in an edit to this column.
# The escapes and rendering rules of divergent.tsv apply unchanged: \n,
# \r and \t are decoded in every column, a control character inside a
# JSON `arg` is spelled \uXXXX, and a rendered `src` or value cannot hold
# a tab, newline or carriage return.
# @repaired: A row counted at a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside a string in Rust
# Under json5's row characters, LF, U+2028 and U+2029, a line character
# inside a single-line string is body: a column, never a row, and not
# `unprintable` when it is in `line.chars` as well. Rust counted a row
# for any row character its cursor stepped over, string body or not, and
# refused any line character inside a single-line string. The last three
# rows are neighbours the same loop decided: a row character outside
# `line.chars` inside a multi-line string, a CR inside a multi-line
# string, and that CR's CRLF control.
string-row-char-control
string-raw-ls
string-raw-ps
string-raw-ls-line-char
string-raw-ps-line-char
string-raw-ls-value
string-raw-ls-then-row
string-raw-nel
string-multi-row-char-only
string-multi-cr
string-multi-crlf-control
# @repaired: No row counted at a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside a multi-line string in Go
# Under json5's line configuration, with the double quote in
# `string.multiChars`, a raw line character inside a multi-line string
# counts a row at any code point, LF, U+2028, U+2029 and a Latin-1
# U+0085 alike, and one in `line.chars` alone resets the column. Go
# tested the line and row sets only below code point 32, and
# TypeScript's own table only below 32 inside its 256 entries, while its
# fallback past the table already answered for any code point. The two
# U+0085 rows, `string-multi-raw-nel` and `string-multi-line-char-nel`,
# pin where TypeScript moved: its answer for a line character from
# U+0020 to U+00FF inside a multi-line string, 1:7 before.
# `string-multi-line-char-ls` is the split that fallback left: 1:4 in
# TypeScript, 1:7 in Go and Rust.
string-multi-row-char-control
string-multi-raw-ls
string-multi-raw-ps
string-multi-raw-ls-ps
string-multi-raw-nel
string-multi-raw-ls-value
string-multi-line-char-nel
string-multi-line-char-ls
# @repaired: An escaped non-ASCII character read as one byte in Go
# The character after the escape character counts one column whatever
# its UTF-8 width, and a `string.escape` mapping of a non-ASCII character
# applies. Go read one byte and stepped one byte, so the column ran ahead
# by the width minus one and the mapping was never found. The astral
# case is not here: `"\😀" y` puts `y` at 7 in TypeScript, two UTF-16
# units, and 6 in Go and Rust, the split under "Column positions for
# astral characters"; and a mapping of an astral character applies in
# Rust alone, the live entry "A `string.escape` key longer than one
# UTF-16 unit" in divergent.tsv.
escape-ascii-control
escape-two-byte
escape-three-byte
escape-two-byte-value
escape-map-ascii-control
escape-map-two-byte
escape-map-three-byte
# @repaired: A non-ASCII `string.replace` key read by its first byte in Go
# A `string.replace` key of one UTF-16 unit applies to that character
# and no other. Go's serialized options keyed the map by the key's first
# BYTE, so a non-ASCII key never applied and its lead byte, read as a
# Latin-1 character, applied instead: `é` (C3 A9) replaced `Ã` (U+00C3).
# Never registered: found while #263 was in review, and repaired with
# the measurement. The last row is the value of the case whose position
# is the live entry "A replaced row character inside a string counts a
# row in Rust".
replace-ascii-control
replace-two-byte
replace-lead-byte
replace-three-byte
replace-ls-json5-value
# @repaired: The `string.replace` map consulted after the escape and control checks in Go
replace-order-control
replace-tab
replace-lf-value
replace-escape-char
